description: Assemble the bounded NPB CG sparse matrix from supplied sparse vectors, then coalesce into canonical CSC order.

source.title: The NAS Parallel Benchmarks
source.role: Algorithm specification; deterministic supplied-vector adaptation; no source implementation reused

contract.operation: Assemble A = sum_i(w_i*x_i*x_i^T) + (0.1-shift)I from caller-supplied sparse vectors, and return its coalesced sparse matrix.
contract.weight_schedule: w_i = 0.1^(i/(n-1)), i=0..n-1; endpoints are exactly 1 and 0.1.
contract.anchor_rule: The caller's vector may omit coordinate i. The benchmark inserts x_i[i]=0.5 if absent, and replaces the supplied value with 0.5 if coordinate i is present.
contract.diagonal_shift: Append (0.1 - shift) to every diagonal coordinate after all vector outer products; shift is supplied in micro-units.
contract.coalescing: All repeated (row,column) coordinates from distinct outer products and diagonal additions are accumulated in vector order; touched coordinates remain present if their final value is zero.
contract.ordering: Return zero-based CSC; columns ascend, and row indices strictly ascend within each column.
contract.sampling: PRNG state and sparse-vector sampling are outside this ABI. Supplied coordinate lists are the deterministic workload input.
contract.source_version_note: The report describes geometric endpoint weights 1 and 0.1. NPB3.4.4 makea uses ratio=pow(0.1,1/n) before each of n vectors, so its last emitted weight is 0.1^((n-1)/n); this profile follows the report's endpoint schedule explicitly.

input.encoding: [n, nonzer, shift_micro, then n records of nonzer (coordinate,value_micro) pairs]
input.vector_value_rule: Each supplied value must be nonzero. Coordinates are zero-based, unique within a vector, and may collide across vectors.

output.encoding: A contiguous little-endian IEEE-754 binary64 vector [n, nnz, col_ptr[n+1], row_index[nnz], values[nnz]]. Structural fields are integral-valued doubles and exactly representable at these bounds.

workspace.meaning: At most 416 raw COO contributions (including anchor-expanded supports and diagonal shifts), plus bounded coalesced CSC pointers, row indices, values, and one five-coordinate vector workspace.
